intro.text: The Closed Ruy Lopez is the classical heart of the opening: long manoeuvring battles where White builds a strong centre and Black chooses between several famous regrouping systems before the central break.
Black develops calmly and prepares to castle, choosing the classical closed Spanish. Both sides manoeuvre for a long time before the central break; plans matter more than early tactics.
The main line of the Closed Ruy Lopez: White protects the centre pawn with the rook, freeing the knight from its defence. Black usually expands on the queenside to gain space and question the bishop.
White protects the centre pawn with a pawn and delays the classical central setup. It is a modern, flexible system that keeps the game slow and avoids the Marshall gambit.
White exchanges the bishop for the knight one move later than in the Exchange Variation, so Black has already committed the bishop to a modest square.
White protects the centre pawn with the queen, keeping the rook free for the d-file. It is an old system with the idea of a quick central advance.
Black gains queenside space and drives the bishop to its best diagonal, from where it aims at Black's kingside. This is the starting point of most classical closed lines.
Against the quiet Martinez setup Black still expands on the queenside. White keeps a flexible centre and can choose between slow manoeuvring and an early queenside strike.
Black protects the centre pawn with a pawn before expanding on the queenside, keeping a compact structure and avoiding some anti-Marshall ideas.
White protects the centre pawn with a pawn after the delayed exchange. Black has the bishop pair; White plans a slow knight manoeuvre and a kingside majority.
White builds a solid central structure with pawns and keeps the bishop's retreat. The play resembles a slow Italian game with Spanish ideas.

intro.text: Black protects the centre pawn with a pawn, the classical way. White now usually prepares a central advance and protects the bishop's retreat with the c-pawn.
Black supports the centre with a pawn in the Martinez structure. Both sides manoeuvre; White can strike on the queenside with the a-pawn to question Black's pawn chain.
Black castles first and keeps the option of an early central strike, a flexible move order in the Martinez structure.

intro.text: Black develops the light-squared bishop to the long diagonal at once, aiming at White's centre and preparing a quick central break.

intro.text: Black castles in the Worrall setup. White plans a quick central advance supported by the queen, and the rook can go to the d-file.
White makes room for the bishop and prepares a big pawn centre. Black usually castles next, transposing to the main classical position.
The main line of the Closed Ruy Lopez: White prepares a central advance and keeps a retreat for the bishop. Black now chooses between the solid classical defence and the Marshall pawn sacrifice.

intro.text: White makes a retreat square for the bishop and prevents Black's knight from jumping forward on the queenside. A flexible, slow system popular at the top level.

intro.text: White prevents Black's light-squared bishop from pinning the knight before deciding on the centre. Black often develops the bishop to the long diagonal in reply.
White strikes at Black's queenside pawn chain at once, trying to open the file for the rook and create weaknesses before Black is fully developed.

intro.text: Black castles and completes kingside development. The game becomes a long manoeuvring battle with typical knight rerouting for both sides.
